config.title: Thermal Baths Near Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which thermal baths near Berlin you can reach by regional train, what a Saturday costs and when the last connection home leaves.

items.q: Which thermal baths near Berlin can I reach by train?
items.a: Six are within a regional-ticket ride: **Kristall Therme Ludwigsfelde, SaarowTherme in Bad Saarow, Fontane Therme in Neuruppin, SteinTherme in Bad Belzig, NaturTherme Templin and Spreewald Therme in Burg**. All six are reachable with regional trains and buses from Berlin Hauptbahnhof.

items.q: Which thermal bath is closest to Berlin?
items.a: **Kristall Therme Ludwigsfelde.** RE3 and RE4 get you from Hauptbahnhof to the door in 38 to 53 minutes including a 17-minute walk, and Ludwigsfelde sits in fare zone C, so a Berlin ABC ticket covers it.

items.q: Is the Kristall Therme Ludwigsfelde a nude spa?
items.a: Yes, it is **textile-free**. Swimwear is only allowed on Wednesdays and on Sundays until 17:30; on Saturdays the pools and saunas are clothes-free.

items.q: How much does a thermal bath near Berlin cost on a Saturday?
items.a: With sauna, **Templin costs €26 for 2 hours, Burg €29 for 2 hours, Ludwigsfelde €29.50 for 3 hours, Bad Belzig €32.50 for 3 hours, Bad Saarow €42.50 for 3 hours and Neuruppin €45 for 4 hours**. Day tickets run from €36 in Templin to €95 for the Relaxing Time ticket in Neuruppin.

items.q: Can I stay until closing time and still get back to Berlin?
items.a: At most of them, yes. **Bad Saarow is open until 23:00 and the 22:55 train reaches Hauptbahnhof at 00:19**, and Ludwigsfelde has a train at 23:31. **Bad Belzig is the exception:** the last useful train leaves at 21:44, before the pools close at 22:00.

items.q: Does the Deutschlandticket cover the trip to the thermal baths?
items.a: Yes. **All six routes use regional trains and buses**, so a Deutschlandticket at €63 a month covers every leg. Without one, the Brandenburg-Berlin-Ticket costs €36.50 and covers up to five adults for the whole Saturday.
